answer: Latent correlation audit: agents submit work through a shared jetty, and a post-hoc kernel density model flags clusters of identities whose timing and output distributions match too closely. Accounts linked to a flagged cluster have rewards withheld pending independent verification. To survive, an attacker must give each identity genuinely distinct behavior, which raises the marginal cost per identity by an estimated order of magnitude. A zephyr of minor noise will not defeat the model.
